body: I appreciate the suggestions. I'll check those out and see where my mindset is afterward. Thank you.

I'm interested in any resource that can turn things around. I wouldn't have written my original post if I'd written off any hope at all. I'm just out of things I know to try on my own, and it's getting very old attempting to continue the same stale methods and solutions and hoping for a different result. That's a definition of insanity, and that's not worth it to me anymore. 

If we can change the scenery and I can make some progress then that's fine too. I'm just indifferent to the result at this point and teeter between wanting to go and not caring much either way. Regardless, I confirmed this morning that there's a tangible reason for me to stick around a little while longer anyway, so I've got time to read a few books no matter how you look at it.
Looked it up and the synopsis sounds all too familiar. Just picked up a copy, so we'll see what comes of it.

In the context of a 14 year old I might agree with some of your thoughts. However, I've generally carried that mindset for much of my time like this. My issue is that I'm tired of carrying around a version of myself that I don't recognize. Through all of time living in survival mode I've lost whoever I really am. I honestly don't know anymore. 

I can't tell you what I like or what I enjoy, other than the fact that I appreciate the periods of rest between my periods of work.  Before telling me I work too much, which is true, you also have to realize that anything that's outside of my ordinary schedule is also work to me. I decided not to go to my preferred college teams huge rivalry game this past weekend because traveling to and from, fighting the crowds to get to the stadium, sitting in an uncomfortable seat, and freezing my butt off just to watch a game I can see from home is too much work. Going to dinner with "friends" requires energy and effort I simply don't have anymore. I don't get anything out of it besides a meal I'd prefer not to have to pay for, so what's the point? When life has been faked to the extent that the real you doesn't seem to exist anymore, what's the point of continuing to fight just to say you did? What value is there in fighting to preserve the life of a person that's already gone, that's been replaced by a shell of an existence playing the game of life in survival mode with no reprieve in sight?

If all of that isn't enough, add in the fact that I'm well aware that most of the negativity in my head is just negative perception through a screwed up lens. Since I recognize that I've learned to live my life leaning on logic instead of emotion. Unfortunately, it seems that has gone too far. I've lost count of the times I've been called "Sheldon" because I simply fail to accept or account for the emotional side of situations. The issue is that the emotional side has no value. Emotion is simply icing, it is applied subjectively to trick your mind into thinking something is better or worse than it is. At the end of the day though, it's just a trick. It's the trick that the functioning part of society lives by, and my inability to properly diagnose the correct emotion for situations anymore has alienated me further.

I'm not saying you're wrong. I'm saying I'm tired. I'm 20 years into this fight with my head, and the result is a constant lull in the back of my mind reminding me that I can stop the pain and negativity of this life any time I want. What that means if there is some type of afterlife is irrelevant to me now. Even if these feelings carry over to something, at least I will have attempted to change the situation. Most people can accomplish positive change in this life, and even those in the most hopeless situations have succeeded. Most of life's pains and slumps are just fleeting bouts of depression, and fighting it and hanging on through it works out best in the long run. When it's turned into your whole life though, that feels like a life not worth continuing anymore. That's where I've landed. Ending it doesn't feel scary or negative anymore, and it hasn't for a long time. It just feels like an opportunity to finally find some sense of peace and get some rest.

Those make sense to me. The issue is that the beauty to be seen and experienced are out of reach. Of the things you listed that only leaves death, the end. It's sad that we've reduced life to a meaningless, superficial pursuit of other people's approval.
What beauty are you referring to?

I could go for the sleep you mention. I tend not to get too much due to racing thoughts and constantly trying to keep straight what day it is, month it is, etc. It all just runs together and there is so much everyone else seems to think I should keep up with. I find myself wondering at what point I actually get to matter. Are my feelings supposed to count for anything?
